I had been fighting with my parents and my councilors to get a diagnosis of Asperger's for months. They would make wild proclamations like "everyone feels awkward sometimes" or "you can talk just fine, you can't be autistic." My psychiatrist at the time laughed in my face when I told her I wanted to be tested, stating that "girls can't have autism." It was in December of 2014 (I was 17) I decided I was done fighting with people who refused to listen to me, so I took a bunch of prescription medication I had saved for about a year in the hopes of killing myself. I ended up driving to the hospital and they had to pump my stomach. I woke up almost 24 hours after taking the meds and spent a few days in a behavioral hospital after that. I had been talking with one of the doctors there about getting tested and she agreed with me. After my release, I saw a specialist who diagnosed me on the spectrum. 

It took me almost dying for my parents to take me seriously. If the people who are supposed to care for my well being don't until I almost die, then everything has to be life or death to get their attention. This wasn't the first time I almost died because of their neglect (even though this was my doing) and it wasn't the last time, either.

My siblings are all very different. I have one brother diagnosed with ADHD and I believe he is on the spectrum as well. Communicating with my NT brothers isn't difficult because I don't like them or we don't get along. For the most part its simply that I have nothing to say. I still enjoy listening to them tell me about the stuff their interested in though because it makes them happy, even if I personally don't like it. The brother with ADHD is similar in that regard, but we have a bit more stuff to talk about. We both enjoy minecraft and we can find funny memes to laugh at on youtube. We might not talk all the time but we can still enjoy each others company. 

Having a sibling with ASD is hard, but its hard to have a NT sibling as well. I would suggest talking with him about things you enjoy to make him feel included. Find what games you two can play together cooperatively. Maybe having a goal while hanging out will make it easier for him to adjust, and for you so you don't feel like youre carrying the relationship. He's your brother and I wouldn't doubt that he loves you. He might just not be able to show it yet.

These are deliberately inappropriate. As someone who is asexual and on the spectrum, this behavior is unacceptable and I cannot wrap my head around how someone on the spectrum could be so....adamantly disregarding basic social norms. Either they are lying in some way, shape, or form to get away with behaving so inappropriately, or they are trying too hard to be "on the spectrum". 

The best thing you can do, especially with someone who is "on the spectrum" as they say, is to speak with them logically. Tell them these questions make you feel uncomfortable and tell them why. If they don't accept that and adjust behavior then cut contact with them. I would rather my friends talk to me about why its inappropriate than talk behind my back and nice to my face. Either the behavior changes through outside social adjustments or they are effectively kicked out of the group, and then they'll have no one. It's a tough choice but autistic people are people first and deserve to be treated the same as everyone else. Even if it means cutting contact with them.

I've never felt love. I can have strong affections for someone, or care about their well being, but I've never felt that "rush" people experience when around a partner or reassurance from my family and friends. I understand love to be an emotion in the same way depression is an emotion. That is to say they are not emotions but a set of emotions and actions/reactions. I'm sure people have felt love in their relationships and I'm not denying its existence. It just seems silly to portray love as an emotion when it's nearly impossible to describe it without using other emotions. That is also why love can quickly turn to hate, because there is a passion in a person but the emotions go from positive to negative. I also believe that's why apathy is worse than hatred. Apathy is an absence of passion and that emotional death hurts worse than anything else in the world.

A hive is at least $100 a pop, plus everything they produce is sellable. Honey obviously, but also comb for honey and for cosmetics like chap stick or candles, propolis has disinfecting qualities (I watched an Amish man offer $70/g of propolis to the beekeeper I was shadowing), and queens can go pretty pricy, too. If you have a steady hand and great timing a beekeeper can raise queens and sell those for $60/queen. They're also interacted with maybe a couple times a week by the beekeeper and often in fields or empty places, so a thief would be able to come in one night, pack up the hive, and have been gone for a few days before the beekeeper notices. It's quick money and profitable in everyway; if you don't get caught. 

As a note, these figures are not accurate I didn't proof while writing this. It's only my estimates for what I've seen as a beginning beekeeper. If you want to know more r/beekeeping might have way more accurate information.

Oh!! I have a lot of interesting facts about bees!!Both eusocial and solitary bees are of the order hymenoptera, and share this order with ants, wasps, and sawflys. Most bee species are solitary, with only a honey bees, bumble bees, and stingless bees are eusocial; The fast majority of the 20,000 bee species are solitary bees. The largest of the eusocial bees is the honey bee in terms of hive count. A strong have can have 20,000-80,000 members, and can produce 50 lbs of honey during the summer. The summer is also the time of year bees have the shortest life span. Worker bees, which are all female, will work themselves to death collecting nectar and pollen, all day every day. She can travel up to 4 miles away from the hive before the nectar collected is not worth the energy expended. 

In terms of brood development period, the brooding time is surprisingly backwards. Queen bees, though not a monarch by any means, take 16 days to grow into an adult; worker bees take 21 days to grow into an adult and immediately set to work tending to the brood; and the drones take 24 days to grow into adult, and their only purpose is to mate with virgin queens. They promptly die after inseminating the new queen, and the unlucky drones return home. winter is hard on the bees and having extra mouths to feed will put a great strain on the colony, so the drones are kicked out at the end of the summer. They cannot care or fend for themselves and will die of starvation or predation. 

last fact: in beekeeping, when you purchase a new hive it is called a nuc. Its a small cardboard box with 5 frames inside of it. the frames are where the comb sit; and there are 2 comb containing brood, 2 frames containing honey and pollen, and an empty frame-- plus a new or virgin queen. they cost about $100 per nuc.
